language: English prose with ordinary mathematical notation
provenance: Retrospective illustrative baselines written after the formal benchmark sources. These were not the original inputs to formalization. Each text is shared by every Litex/Lean route for that case; it must not be tuned to improve a reported factor.

new-round/sqrt_two_irrational.text: sqrt(2) is irrational. Otherwise write sqrt(2) = p/q in lowest terms, with p an integer and q a positive integer. Squaring gives p^2 = 2q^2, so p is even. Write p = 2k; then q^2 = 2k^2, so q is even too. This contradicts gcd(p,q) = 1.

new-round/set_union_inter_distrib.text: For subsets A, B, D of the reals, A ∪ (B ∩ D) = (A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ D), by the distributive law for sets.

new-round/set_diff_union.text: For subsets A, B, D of the reals, A ∖ (B ∪ D) = (A ∖ B) ∩ (A ∖ D): membership on either side means belonging to A and to neither B nor D.

new-round/set_inter_monotone.text: For subsets A, B, D of the reals, if A ⊆ B then A ∩ D ⊆ B ∩ D. An element of A ∩ D belongs to B and D.

new-round/function_mem_range.text: For f : R → R and x ∈ R, f(x) belongs to the range of f, with witness x.

new-round/integer_division_decomposition.text: For an integer a and a positive integer d, a = d⌊a/d⌋ + (a mod d), by quotient-remainder decomposition.

new-round/integer_divisibility.text: For integers a and c with c ≠ 0, c divides ac, since ac = ca.

new-round/finite_cardinality.text: The set {1,2,3} has three elements, by counting its distinct entries.

new-round/powerset_cardinality.text: A finite set A of natural numbers has 2^|A| subsets: for each element independently choose whether to include it.

new-round/factorial_positive.text: For every natural number n, n! > 0, by positivity of the factorial.

new-round/derivative_square_at_three.text: For f(x) = x^2 on R, f'(3) = 6, since f'(x) = 2x and 2·3 = 6.

new-round/pair_reconstruction.text: Every pair p ∈ R × R equals the pair of its first and second coordinates, by the pair reconstruction law.

new-round/continuity_square_at_three.text: The function x ↦ x^2 on R is continuous at 3, by continuity of powers.

multi-step/sum_sq_zero.text: For real x,y, if x^2+y^2 = 0 then x = y = 0: both squares are nonnegative, so each square is zero.

multi-step/positive_ratio.text: For a positive real x, x+1 > 0, hence x/(x+1) > 0 by positivity of the numerator and denominator.

multi-step/mul_cancel.text: For real x,y, if 2x = 2y then x = y, by cancelling the nonzero factor 2.

multi-step/sq_plus_one_pos.text: For every real x, x^2+1 > 0, because x^2 ≥ 0 and 1 > 0.

multi-step/sum_sq_ge_two_mul.text: For real x,y, x^2+y^2 ≥ 2xy, since 0 ≤ (x-y)^2 = x^2+y^2-2xy.

multi-step/even_witness_above.text: For every positive integer n there is a positive even integer m > n. Take m = 2n; it is positive, exceeds n, and is divisible by 2.

multi-step/nat_succ_lt_two_mul.text: Every positive integer n satisfies 2n > n, since 2n-n = n > 0.

statement-forms/prop_definition_witness.scope: definition and witness; Lean unfolds the predicate
statement-forms/prop_definition_witness.text: An integer a is odd if a = 2t+1 for some integer t. The number 7 is odd, with witness t = 3.

statement-forms/odd_shift.scope: definition, statement and witness proof; Lean unfolds the predicate
statement-forms/odd_shift.text: An integer a is odd if a = 2t+1 for some integer t. If an integer n is odd, write n = 2k+1. Then 3n+2 = 3(2k+1)+2 = 2(3k+2)+1, so 3n+2 is odd with witness 3k+2.

statement-forms/reciprocal_tends_to_zero.scope: sequence definition, statement and proof; Lean inlines the sequence
statement-forms/reciprocal_tends_to_zero.text: Let a(n) = 1/n for positive integers n. For every real ε > 0 there is a positive integer n with a(n) < ε. By the Archimedean property choose n > 1/ε; then a(n) = 1/n < ε.

statement-forms/set_union_subset_eq.text: For subsets A,B of the reals, if A ⊆ B then A ∪ B = B. Every element of A or B belongs to B, and every element of B belongs to A ∪ B.

declarations/guarded_function.text: For nonzero real x define bench_recip(x) = 1/x. Then bench_recip(2) = 1/2 by substitution.
